items.summary: Emergency department (ED) decision-making relies on heterogeneous clinical information, including patient history, vital signs, laboratory results, and electrocardiograms (ECGs). Vision--language models (VLMs) can jointly process these modalities, but strong predictive performance does not necessarily imply meaningful use of the correct patient's ECG. We term this failure mode ECG Mirage: apparent multimodal capability without useful dependence on patient-specific ECG information. We distinguish two forms: ECG neglect, where ECGs provide little predictive benefit, and ECG confusion, where matched ECGs outperform no-image inputs but not mismatched ECGs. To evaluate these behaviours, we compare predictions obtained with matched ECGs, outcome-discordant mismatched ECGs, and no-image inputs while holding the clinical text and prediction targets fixed. Across four VLMs on MDS-ED, matched ECGs provide no consistent advantage for either ICU admission or clinical deterioration prediction. We then train four restricted visual prompts using supervised learning followed by conditional direct preference optimisation, while keeping the VLM backbone frozen. The resulting models achieve balanced accuracies of 70.6% for ICU admission and 67.5% for deterioration and increase the matched-versus-mismatched performance gap to approximately 16.5 and 5.5 percentage points, respectively. Overall, our study identifies ECG Mirage in multimodal clinical prediction and introduces visual prompt tuning as an efficient mitigation strategy.
items.title: ECG Mirage: Revealing and Mitigating the Underutilisation of ECGs in Vision-Language Models for Clinical Prediction

items.summary: Long-context large language model inference is increasingly limited by prefill, where dense self-attention processes the entire prompt before generation begins. Sparse block selection can reduce this cost, but a block centroid may hide a highly relevant token among many irrelevant ones. We call this failure mode mean dilution and propose RBS-Attention, a training-free sparse-prefill method with two complementary selection branches. A centroid base branch captures average relevance, while a rescue branch uses the maximum key-block radius and its prompt-, layer-, and head-dependent distribution to identify blocks at risk of underestimation. Independently thresholding the two branches and combining their masks controls the contribution of rescue blocks while preserving regular block-sparse FlashAttention execution. On H100 GPUs, RBS-Attention achieves 20.65$\times$ standalone prefill-attention speedup, 11.92$\times$ vLLM prefill-attention speedup, and 5.97$\times$ end-to-end time-to-first-token speedup at 128K on Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-FP8. On the dense Qwen3-32B model, it obtains 88.65 overall RULER accuracy versus 89.52 for dense attention; LongBench-v2, InfiniteBench, and Video-MME provide additional quality evaluation. Supporting experiments measure actual retention, compare selectors at matched density, and characterize block-size, threshold, and memory behavior. Together, these results support radius-adaptive dual-branch selection as an effective approach to long-context prefill.
items.title: RBS-Attention: Radius-Bounded Sparse Prefill for Long-Context Large Language Models

items.summary: This paper refines the finiteness conjecture for stability architectures and establishes the strongest currently provable results. A stability claim is treated as a profile specifying the object, state space, evolution, perturbation class, projection, failure region, time horizon, and obstructing gap or invariant. An architecture abstracts the structural core: the category of state spaces, the operator class, the gap functional, and the transport obstruction. The paper proves that stability cannot be classified from the trajectory map alone; the full profile matters. For linear systems, there are exactly three distinct architectures: dissipative, geometric or gradient, and Hamiltonian. For model-theoretic stability, the classification is finite and known: stability, NIP, simplicity, and rosiness. This logical classification is an analogy, not a direct translation to dynamics. For Hamiltonian systems, conditional finiteness identifies five candidate mechanisms: KAM persistence, Nekhoroshev confinement, Trojan resonance-gap suppression, symmetry constraint, and barrier obstruction. For statistical systems, four candidates appear: uniform, partial, and non-uniform hyperbolicity, plus rate conditions. In both cases, finiteness follows only if the lists are exhaustive, which remains conjectural. The paper also proves an intra-architecture transfer theorem, a qualified cross-architecture rigidity theorem, and a proposition on overlapping architectures. Transfer works within a shared architecture because estimates depend only on structural data. Rigidity blocks transfer between structurally distinct architectures unless additional structure exists. Overlap is possible, allowing multiple stability mechanisms and multiple failure routes. The general classification problem is undecidable, proved by reduction from the halting problem. Limitations include autonomous, finite-dimensional, smooth dynamics; time-dependent, infinite-dimensional, non-smooth, and nonlinear cases remain open. The consequences concern analog laboratories, engineering design by architecture selection, and a finite core of stability theory. The central message is that the finiteness conjecture is not vacuous: it holds where testable, while full generality awaits resolution of the exhaustiveness conjectures.
items.title: Stability Architectures: A Finite Classification of Provable Cases

items.summary: Memory segmentation is thought to arise from rapid decorrelation in neural activity, often quantified by Euclidean distance or cosine angle. Although these metrics detect a transition, they do not reveal how the new state relates to the repertoire represented by the neural manifold. This matters because neuromodulators that drive state transitions also alter excitability, and learning may repurpose existing representations or create new ones. Here, I introduce a geometric decomposition that separates changes attributable to gain modulation of a nearby manifold state from movement within the manifold and genuine off-manifold displacement. The approach uses the radial axis of neural population activity to partition the normal space of a local manifold region. A central challenge is identifiability: given only a static reference manifold and a single test state, neither the state from which a perturbation began nor its gain magnitude and mechanistic decomposition can generally be recovered uniquely. I therefore formulate identifiability as a cascade of geometric gates specifying when each component can be interpreted. The gates distinguish structural failures, including the absence of a local chart or incorrect intrinsic dimensionality, from estimation error and systematic bias caused by reference sampling, tangent-frame error, gain-axis misalignment, anchor displacement, and poor ratio conditioning. Simulations show that neighborhood size, curvature, sampling density, ambient dimension, and noise act through a small set of geometric quantities. The framework specifies when assignments to gain or novelty are identifiable, how they become biased, and which diagnostics reveal the relevant failure regime. By quantifying the nature rather than only the magnitude of neural state change, it provides a clear, readily interpretable framework for evaluating mechanisms of neural state transitions.
items.title: Identifying Neural State Changes due to Gain versus Off-Manifold Displacement

items.summary: README – Coarse-Grained Molecular Dynamics (CGMD) Simulations of PIEZO1 and TRPM4 Overview This dataset contains coarse-grained molecular dynamics (CGMD) simulations of the mechanosensitive ion channel PIEZO1 and the non-mechanoprotective ion channel TRPM4 embedded in lipid bilayers. The simulations comprise 500 ns of equilibrium followed by membrane stretching simulations designed to investigate how PIEZO1's distinctive triskelion blade architecture redistributes mechanical stress and preserves membrane integrity. All simulations were performed using GROMACS with the Martini 3 force field. Independent replicate simulations (n = 3) were conducted for each system to ensure statistical robustness and reproducibility. Simulation Details Parameter Description Molecular dynamics engine : GROMACS v2021.2 Force field : Martini 3 Membrane model : Lipid bilayer containing either PIEZO1 or TRPM4 Equilibration : 500 ns Stretching simulations : Three independent replicates (n = 3); 50 ns Simulation temperature, pressure, and all additional parameters are provided in the accompanying simulation input files (.mdp) and described in the associated publication. Biological Significance PIEZO1 is a mechanosensitive ion channel whose unique triskelion blade architecture protects cellular membranes from mechanical failure. Its extended peripheral blades redistribute mechanical stress across the lipid bilayer, reducing localized stress accumulation and delaying membrane rupture during mechanical loading. This dataset enables quantitative investigation of how membrane protein architecture influences membrane mechanics, force redistribution, and mechanoprotection using coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations. Dataset Structure 1. Equilibrium Simulations These simulations characterize the equilibrated membrane environment surrounding each ion channel before mechanical loading. Simulation length: 500 ns PIEZO1_equilibrium.pdb PIEZO1_equilibrium.xtc TRPM4_equilibrium.pdb TRPM4_equilibrium.xtc 2. Membrane Stretching Simulations Following equilibration, membrane stretch was induced using semi-isotropic pressure coupling, with −5 bar applied in the membrane plane (x–y) while maintaining +1 bar normal to the bilayer (z-axis) using the Parrinello–Rahman barostat. PIEZO1 PIEZO1_Stretch_R1.pdb PIEZO1_Stretch_R1.xtc PIEZO1_Stretch_R1.edr PIEZO1_Stretch_R2.pdb PIEZO1_Stretch_R2.xtc PIEZO1_Stretch_R2.edr PIEZO1_Stretch_R3.pdb PIEZO1_Stretch_R3.xtc PIEZO1_Stretch_R3.edr TRPM4 TRPM4_Stretch_R1.pdb TRPM4_Stretch_R1.xtc TRPM4_Stretch_R1.edr TRPM4_Stretch_R2.pdb TRPM4_Stretch_R2.xtc TRPM4_Stretch_R2.edr TRPM4_Stretch_R3.pdb TRPM4_Stretch_R3.xtc TRPM4_Stretch_R3.edr Data Usage The trajectory (.xtc) and coordinate (.pdb) files can be analysed using standard molecular dynamics software, including GROMACS, VMD, and PyMOL. The (.edr) files are also provided for energy calculations and to be utilized -b 0 -e 50000 (time 0 - 50 ns) These simulations support quantitative analyses described in the associated publication. PIEZO1 safeguards membranes under mechanical stress via permeation-independent structural adaptation and calcium-dependent cytoskeletal reinforcement. Cell Press Blue. (2026). https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cpblue.2026.100128
items.title: PIEZO1 safeguards membranes under mechanical stress using MD simulation

items.summary: A characteristic corrugated surface morphology of Nb films on Cu is identified, with mesoscopic features comparable to the London penetration depth and coherence length, and its impact on superconducting radio frequency cavity performance metrics is examined. Magnetic field enhancement factors and superheating field suppression factors are calculated within the London model for a representative corrugated geometry. These results demonstrate that roughness trends derived from buffered chemical polished and electropolished Nb cavities do not capture the impact of nanoscale surface morphology on SRF Nb thin film performance, as even surfaces that possess low average roughness can contain geometric features that generate substantial local field enhancement and significantly suppress the Bean Livingston barrier. The influence of surface roughness on impurity diffusion is also investigated, which highlights the roles of increased surface area and local geometric confinement in modifying near surface impurity distributions. Tracking the effect of impurity diffusion on the evolution of magnetic field enhancement, we show that geometrically confined impurity distributions can mitigate nanoscale magnetic field enhancement substantially.
items.title: Failure of Conventional Roughness Metrics in Assessing Field-Limiting Mesoscopic Topography in SRF Nb Films on Cu

items.summary: Read the 74-page Split-Zero paper . Complete LaTeX, cumulative sources, citations and checks ; results and exact proof locators ; matching GitHub source edition . The Split-Zero programme represents finite zero-divisor classes of the completed Riemann zeta function by polynomials in an arithmetic theta-source Hilbert space. The metric on the observation kernel is obtained by minimizing over all original polynomial representatives. This edition calculates how that metric changes with polynomial degree. It gives every Christoffel–Darboux covariance entry, including reflected-node collisions and divided derivatives; retains the full correction after coefficient compression; and expresses the four-cutoff determinant ratio as a product of exact degree-step factors. The paired quartet relation proves a strict finite kernel contraction. Its magnitude at the unresolved large-degree kq scale is not evaluated, and no RH conclusion is claimed. Programme citations in the paper are clickable links to actual public proof sources, with exact locations where available. The same source links are included in the three complete cumulative LaTeX successors. The source archive includes a machine-readable link registry and restores two previously unpublished cited proofs. Older cumulative citations still needing an exact source match remain explicitly identified in that registry; no guessed destination is presented as verified. Classical sources retain their human authorship: Gernot Akemann and Graziano Vernizzi, Characteristic Polynomials of Complex Random Matrix Models , Nuclear Physics B 660 (2003), 532–556 ; the named authors of the NIST DLMF orthogonal-polynomial chapter ; and Jack Sherman and Winifred J. Morrison, Adjustment of an Inverse Matrix Corresponding to a Change in One Element of a Given Matrix (1950) . The last citation is historical and bibliographically checked; the rank-one calculation used here is proved directly. Earlier programme proofs remain separately credited. The reader contains ten complete proof bodies. The new CD and degree-step checkers pass 779 exact finite checks in each of ordinary and optimized Python, with 13 intended failure controls in each mode. These checks do not sample the actual period matrix or establish a large-degree asymptotic. The three large cumulative LaTeX manuscripts have not been freshly compiled in this edition. The 98 earlier standalone papers and archives remain. To respect Zenodo's 100-file limit, the preceding result index is retained byte-for-byte as predecessor062/RESULT_INDEX.json in the new source ZIP. Its original separate download also remains in the preceding immutable edition. Existing authorship, rights notices and access conditions are preserved. This successor does not claim that unfinished parallel-task work has been incorporated.
items.title: Split-Zero cohomology: exact degree changes in the arithmetic kernel metric

items.summary: This paper offers a critical analysis of the European Union as a model of regional integration and examines its contribution to peace and to the effectiveness of the United Nations system. Set against the background of the failure of the League of Nations, the study argues that the post-1945 international order has endured largely because it is supported by strong regional institutions. Using the EU as the primary case study, the paper contends that by institutionalizing peace within Europe through economic interdependence, binding law, and supranational governance, the EU has created a zone of stability that reduces the burden on global governance structures. Furthermore, the paper analyzes how the EU functions as a support pillar for the United Nations under Chapter VIII of the UN Charter. Through financial contributions, peacekeeping partnerships, and coordinated diplomacy, the EU has reinforced multilateralism and provided capacity for conflict management and development. A comparative perspective is also drawn with other regional bodies such as ECOWAS to demonstrate a broader pattern of regional-global cooperation. The paper concludes that the longevity of the United Nations, compared to the League of Nations, can be partly explained by this two-level architecture of global and regional governance. While the EU’s support for the UN is substantial, it is also inconsistent, as internal EU divisions sometimes undermine collective action. Ultimately, the study shows that effective regional integration is a critical condition for sustaining peace and strengthening the United Nations system.
items.title: The European Union and Regional Integration: A Critical Analysis of Peacebuilding and Support for the United Nations System

items.summary: ElectromagneticFields v0.9.0 Diff since v0.8.0 Breaking Changes Everything here that requires a change to calling code, and what to do about it. The sections below give the reasoning; this is the checklist. @code , its seven per-preset variants, code and load_equilibrium are gone. Generated code is no longer injected into a module. Build a field by calling FieldFunctions(equ) , which returns a value: it can be constructed inside a function, stored, and passed to a vector field through a problem's parameters , none of which the old module injection allowed. The ~450 scalar functions are ~41 generics returning tensors, each taking the field first. B¹(t, q) becomes B♯(field, t, q)[1] and dAᵢdxⱼ(t, q) becomes DA♭(field, t, q)[i, j] . The names use the musical isomorphisms — ♭ covariant, ♯ contravariant, ♮ physical, the bare letter the magnitude — and Changed below has the full old-to-new table. Every one of the ~444 old scalar values is an entry of one of the new tensors. The per-field submodules are flattened into the package. Solovev.ITER() is SolovevEquilibriumITER() , ThetaPinch.init() is ThetaPinchEquilibrium() , and so on for every field; Solovev.ITER(xpoint = true) and its siblings are gone in favour of the named X-point constructors. The coordinate helpers X , Y , Z , R , r , θ , ϕ and r² are package-level generics and deliberately not exported — reach them as ElectromagneticFields.R or through coordinates(field) . periodicity is no longer answered or exported by this package. GeometricBase.periodic(equ) gives one Bool per coordinate instead, and a chart with no method for it raises a MethodError when a field is built from it, deliberately. Code that assembled a (xmin, xmax) tuple from rangemin / rangemax behind a single flag must now build it from periodic and the bounds. periodicity = periodic(field) is silently wrong , not an error: a three-element Bool vector destructures to (false, false) . parameters(field) for a Solov'ev equilibrium now includes the coefficient vector c . A₃ reads it, so it travels with the other parameters instead of being frozen into the code. A field rebuilt after clear_field_cache!() is equal to a few ULP, not bit for bit. Compare two builds of one field with a tolerance rather than == . SymEngine is no longer a dependency ; Symbolics, StaticArrays, GeometricBase and ConstructionBase are. The Julia floor stays 1.10. Added Aqua.jl runs as part of the test suite , in test/aqua_tests.jl , which calls Aqua.test_all . This package carried no package-level quality check of any kind before, so all eight — method ambiguities, unbound type parameters, undefined exports, the agreement between Project.toml and test/Project.toml , stale dependencies, [compat] bounds, type piracy and persistent tasks — start from a clean pass rather than from a list of known failures. Two of them cover something this package does structurally. test_piracies covers the eight methods added to GeometricBase's periodic , functions and parameters , each of which dispatches on a type defined here; a new chart family brings a periodic method with it, so the property outlasts any list of the sites. test_undefined_exports covers an export list dominated by the musical-isomorphism accessors, which are defined across src/analytic/ rather than beside the export. The test suite has a test/Project.toml of its own , carrying Aqua, CairoMakie, LinearAlgebra, SafeTestsets, StaticArrays and Test, each with a [compat] bound. The [extras] and [targets] sections of the package's Project.toml are gone with it, together with the CairoMakie bound that belonged to them. Test dependencies that only [extras] declared carried no bounds at all, which is what Aqua.test_deps_compat reports. Changed The symbolic engine is replaced from SymEngine.jl to Symbolics.jl. Dependencies change: SymEngine is removed, Symbolics, StaticArrays, GeometricBase and ConstructionBase are added. Julia floor stays 1.10. GeometricBase is there for the generic names functions ,
items.title: JuliaPlasma/ElectromagneticFields.jl: v0.9.0

items.summary: Embarrassingly parallel workloads, such as parameter sweeps, Monte Carlo simulations, and hyperparameter searches, are pervasive in research computing, yet running a single experiment across a mix of laptops, lab servers, cloud virtual machines (VMs), and high-performance computing (HPC) clusters still demands ad hoc Secure Shell (SSH) tunnels, port forwarding, and scheduler-specific scripts. We present DART, a job distributor that turns any such mix of machines into a single shared queue. DART pairs a Dockerized job server with a one-line worker command-line interface (CLI); a hosted Hub automates reverse tunneling, worker authentication, and public endpoint provisioning, so collaborators on any network, including those behind network address translation (NAT) or using a personal laptop, can join an experiment with a single API-key and no firewall changes. This makes DART especially effective for researchers who combine Advanced Cyberinfrastructure Coordination Ecosystem: Services & Support (ACCESS)-provisioned HPC resources [1] with institutional clusters and personal workstations, federating all resources under one queue with no per-site configuration. All communication is encrypted end-to-end, and access is controlled through API-key authentication and a personal identification number (PIN)-protected dashboard. Researchers create experiments, define parameter grids, and monitor jobs entirely from a web dashboard; a work-conserving scheduler dispatches jobs on demand, exploits resource heterogeneity, and automatically re-queues failures. In a real-world deployment of 37,720 jobs across 68 heterogeneous machines spanning an institutional HPC cluster, a national ACCESS resource, and personal computers, the observed run completed in approximately eight days. DART’s dynamic allocation achieved a simulation-derived 35× speedup over static partitioning (≈4 days vs. ≈139 days), reducing a multi-month workload to days.
items.title: DART: Distributed Assignment of Research Tasks for Heterogeneous Compute Environments

items.summary: As LLM capabilities have expanded, multi-agent communication has emerged as an increasingly active area of research. Prevailing protocols often adopt rigid structures that introduce coordination bottlenecks and can degrade as the number of agents increases. We introduce Proxifield, a round-adaptive multi-agent protocol with decentralized agent decision-making that constructs sparse communication graphs from the evolving semantic proximity of agents. Without model training or a centralized planner, Proxifield connects agents using four routing signals derived at inference time: direct address, information needs, plan alignment, and information complementarity. We compare Proxifield with two representative coordination baselines, a centralized Star protocol and a decentralized Shared Context protocol, across two domains: Drone Search and Rescue and the collective-reasoning benchmark HiddenBench. We first ablate base-model capability and find that, in both domains, the performance of Proxifield improves with model size (35B -> 397B parameter model) and Proxifield outperforms all baselines at the largest scale. As team size increases, Proxifield's task-reward advantage over Star widens from 5.4% at (N=5) to 53.0% at (N=25) and 59.5% at (N=50), while Shared Context consistently underperforms both protocols. Proxifield is also substantially more robust to permanent agent failure, retaining 73.6% of its no-failure task reward under the most severe condition, compared with 58.3% for Shared Context and 38.8% for Star. These results demonstrate that decentralized, semantically adaptive routing can improve the scalability and fault tolerance of multi-agent systems.
items.title: Proxifield: Decentralized Multi-Agent Communication through Semantic Proximity

items.summary: This paper asks a narrow question. Lyapunov stability, geometric stability, and statistical stability are all described as spectral-gap properties. The gaps act on different operators, live on different spaces, and survive different perturbations. The informal habit of treating them as one nested hierarchy is correct for convex wells and hyperbolic sinks. It is not correct as a statement about dynamical systems in general. The paper replaces that habit with a comparison theorem. A stability claim is a profile: an evolution, a perturbation class, a projection, and a failure set. Comparative type can change when the map is held fixed and only the projection changes. Three statistical properties are kept distinct. The first is weak continuity of an invariant measure under perturbation. The second is a spectral gap of a transfer or Fokker–Planck operator on a named function space. The third is differentiability of the measure in the perturbation parameter. These three can hold together. They can also separate. The proved implications are scoped. A positive Hessian implies Lyapunov stability of a mechanical equilibrium and a dissipative Jacobian gap for a gradient flow. A hyperbolic sink gives weak continuity of a Dirac family and does not give mixing on a positive-dimensional density space. Uniform hyperbolicity gives a transfer-operator gap on an anisotropic space and, in the perturbation class of Keller and Liverani, weak continuity of an SRB family. Partial hyperbolicity yields a gap only after restriction to the hyperbolic factor. Nonuniform hyperbolicity with a Young tower yields a slower, tail-controlled rate and is compatible with instability of almost every orbit. A prescribed decay for a piecewise expanding map or a hypocoercive generator need not come from any hyperbolic splitting. Architectural estimates do not transfer between structurally distinct operator classes. In one linear-quadratic noise model the three classical tests return the same number. In a double well they separate. The paper does not claim that statistical mechanisms are finite, and it does not prove that averaging a frequency-gap Hamiltonian system produces a kinetic spectral gap.
items.title: Which Spectral Gaps Imply Which: Lyapunov, Geometric, and Statistical Criteria

items.summary: Abstract The stability of the banking sector is fundamental to economic growth and financial system resilience, particularly in developing economies such as Nigeria.  However, and sadly enough, global, recent and recurring failure risks and collapses of banks which have been blamed on poor external audit qualities, are counter-productive to national economic development.  Therefore, the broad objective of this study was to study the effect of audit quality on failure risks of listed deposit money banks in Nigeria between the period 2009 and 2024. This study adopted both descriptive and ex-post facto research designs.  Using secondary data extracted from audited financial reports of 11 censored (from a population of 11) deposit money banks listed on the Nigerian Exchange Group, (NGX), and analyzing one hundred and seventy-six firm year observations using regression with Driscoll–Kraay standard errors analysis technique, the findings revealed that audit firm size (AUFS) significantly improve bank Z score, [coef. = 0.638 (p-value = 0.005)], audit report timeliness (ARTIME) significantly reduces bank Z score [coef. = −0.400 (p-value = audit committee diligence (ACDI) revealed a positive insignificant effect respectively on Z score of listed deposit money banks in Nigeria during the period under consideration. Based on the above findings, it was concluded that audit quality in the Nigerian banking sector is not uniformly effective, rather, its effect on bank failure risks is selective, with only specific audit mechanisms demonstrating the capacity to significantly enhance financial solvency, thereby suggesting that the effectiveness of external audit as a safeguard against bank failure risks depend not merely on its presence, but likely on factors such as depth, credibility, and functional execution of its key components.   this study concluded that audit.  Consequently, this study recommended among others, that listed deposit money banks in Nigeria, alongside regulators and external auditors, should prioritize substantive governance quality, auditor competence and independence, rigorous audit execution, timely financial reporting, risk-sensitive audit remuneration, coordinated assurance mechanisms, and proactive internal control systems over mere procedural compliance, in order to strengthen transparency, reinforce market confidence, and enhance long term financial stability in line with Agency theory. Keywords: Audit Quality, Failure Risks of Listed Deposit Money Banks, Bank Z-Score, Agency Theory.
tags: Audit Quality, Failure Risks of Listed Deposit Money Banks, Bank Z-Score, Agency Theory.
items.title: Audit Quality and Failure Risks of Listed Deposit Money Banks In Nigeria

items.summary: Code and data to reproduce all analyses and the figure in O'Dea et al. (2026) "Failure of a tropical upwelling rapidly collapsed Panama's anchoveta fishery and its exports". Includes Python scripts for the reef-logger upwelling indices, the bay-wide composite index, the observer set records, the anchoveta length and weight series, the unified 1956 to 2025 landings series, and the main figure together with every statistic reported in the paper. Data include weekly sonde casts from the three deep central stations of the Bay of Panama, continuous reef temperature loggers from the Gulf of Panama running since 1995, the Copernicus Marine Service biogeochemical reanalysis of net primary production (1994 to 2026), anchoveta and thread herring landings spliced from the digitised national stock assessment (1956 to 2014) and the ARAP landings register (2015 to 2025, 332,610 records across 206 taxa), 3,077 onboard observer purse-seine set records (2017 to 2025), 645 dockside proximate assays of landed anchoveta (2016 to 2025), and fish oil and fishmeal export tabulations from INEC customs statistics (1997 to 2025). The archive is self-contained and rebuilds the figure and all reported statistics from the raw sources whenever the derived and figures directories are deleted. Instructions for use, including execution order, software dependencies, directory structure, the provenance of every source and the known caveats, are in README.md. Data are released under CC BY 4.0 and code under the MIT Licence.
items.title: Code and data for: Failure of a tropical upwelling rapidly collapsed Panama's anchoveta fishery and its exports

items.summary: When language models reason in chain-of-thought or exchange free-text intermediates, they serialize structured information into natural language. How much tree-structured compositional content survives this bottleneck? We propose a round-trip protocol that answers this question empirically for tree-structured expressions. A generator converts a procedurally generated arithmetic expression into a word problem, a separate extractor recovers the expression from the word problem alone, and symbolic equivalence provides an exact oracle. Evaluating all pairwise combinations of sixteen models yields a communication matrix whose marginals separate generation quality from extraction quality. Three main findings emerge. First, the channel is lossy and asymmetric: swapping which model generates and which extracts shifts accuracy by up to 60.4 points, and the best pair reaches 92.9% by combining different models on each end rather than the same model on both. Second, at least 73.6% of round-trip failures originate at generation, and difficulty is driven by tree structure (operator count, depth, right-branching) rather than model family. Third, the channel is trainable: ~3600 fine-tuning examples that share the evaluation's operators and tree shapes lift every open-weight model above untrained Gemini-3.1-Pro, an upper bound under matched semantics. A disjoint-domain regime with new operators and vocabulary also raises every open-weight model, confirming the gain is not an artifact of matched semantics, though a gap to the frontier remains. Together these results identify tree-structured expression serialization as a primary limiting factor when models communicate hierarchical structure through natural language.
items.title: The Communication Bottleneck: A Round-Trip Study of Tree-Structured Expression Serialization in Language Models

items.summary: Abstract Distributed version control preserves source states, ancestry, branching, merging, and collaboration with extraordinary success. It does not ordinarily require engineering intent, failed approaches, claim scope, verification evidence, residual disagreement, or continuation state to exist as typed repository objects. Those records instead tend to be distributed across commit prose, review systems, issue trackers, CI logs, artifact stores, chat, and human memory. This disclosure explores a broader version-control model for software developed by humans and agents without claiming that content addressing, provenance, attestations, change-oriented versioning, or agent memory are new in isolation. Gemel models an evidence-bearing change : a content-addressed relation from an exact input state to an exact output state, linked to intent, operations, producer provenance, claims, evidence, residuals, verification scope, and causal context. Trajectories preserve completed, rejected, interrupted, superseded, and inconclusive work. Claims remain declarations rather than stored truth; support and readiness are derived conservatively from evidence, residuals, freshness, supersession, and policy. Context manifests and checkpoints provide bounded continuation surfaces without requiring private reasoning transcripts. The inspected Rust reference implementation defines deterministic canonical encoding, BLAKE3-256 identities, immutable objects, mutable refs, rebuildable indexes, 24 object families, Git-carried exchange, deterministic Git projection, semantic indexing, native and hosted synchronization, agent queries, policy checks, and an FRF court runner. For this paper, the supplied source archive was independently built in a clean temporary directory and cargo test --all-targets completed 236 tests with zero failures. This result is implementation-specific conformance evidence. It is not evidence that Gemel improves developer productivity, agent reliability, or industrial outcomes. Gemel composes with the Forensic Residual Framework (FRF) as an evidence plane and with FRF-Fuzz as a discovery plane. The paper situates that composition against Git facilities, patch algebra, provenance models, software-supply-chain attestations, reproducible builds, software archives, event sourcing, rationale capture, and agent memory. It discloses alternative embodiments and defines falsifiable evaluations for handoff quality, repeated-error reduction, evidence freshness, reconciliation, interoperability, context cost, storage overhead, and longitudinal fuzzing. Its principal claim is architectural: software history can be represented as an engineering graph in which source state, intent, evidence, residual uncertainty, negative knowledge, and continuation state possess explicit identity and scope. Whether that representation earns its operational cost remains an empirical question. Keywords distributed version control; Git; agentic software development; evidence engineering; provenance; content addressing; Merkle DAG; software agents; developmental trajectories; negative knowledge; residual primacy; FRF; FRF-Fuzz; reproducibility; software archaeology; semantic lineage; source provenance; event sourcing.
items.title: Gemel: Evidence-Native Version Control for Agentic Software Development - Longitudinal Engineering Memory, Residual-Aware Change Graphs, Git Interchange, and Reproducible Agent Handoffs

items.summary: Behavioral failures can make a transformer appear to lack a world model even when it has learned faithful representations of its environment. We demonstrate this in TaxiGPT, a transformer trained on random walks through Manhattan whose failures have been interpreted as evidence of an incoherent internal map. Through mechanistic analysis and causal interventions, we show that the model represents intersections and streets, tracks its position, and uses a goal compass to navigate. We trace its failures to interference between superposed intersection features, which disrupts localization within the internal map. Affordance packing, which groups representations of intersections with the same legal moves, helps limit the consequences of these errors. Finally, we propose mechanistic indicators that we use to compare models and show that world-modeling capacities emerge at different stages of training. Our findings motivate a shift from asking whether a model has a world model to mechanistically studying its world modeling: the interacting capacities through which it represents its environment and uses those representations to guide behavior.
items.title: World Modeling in Transformers

items.summary: LLM-based multi-agent systems generate collaboration traces that record how agents plan tasks, verify intermediate results, and repair failures. Reusing these procedures requires preserving an action's prerequisites and the outputs needed by subsequent agents. Our empirical studies show that grouping these dependencies into functional memory units improves their retention, while connecting units increases retrieval of the units and links jointly required by a task. The preferred combination of units also changes between instructions and checklists, even when each combination's content is fixed across formats. Updating choices from the outcomes of each combination and format pairing outperforms scoring combinations and formats separately. These findings motivate MACE, a memory-agent co-evolution framework that adapts memory organization and agent memory use through execution feedback. Its MemGoG structure represents functional units as subgraphs of related conditions, actions, and outputs, connecting them through support, conflict, and repair relations. MACE Loop selects task-relevant units and relations within a memory budget and provides each agent with instructions or checklists for its current operation. It records the selected units, presentation formats, agent outputs, and task outcomes to update unit scores and relations for retrieval and inform subsequent presentation choices. Across eight benchmarks, MACE outperforms ten baselines with an average score of 81.11%, compared with 78.97% for the strongest baseline, SAGE.
items.title: MACE: Memory-Agent Co-Evolution with Adaptive Memory Graphs for Multi-Agent Systems

items.summary: Anticoncentration is a key ingredient in complexity theoretic arguments for quantum advantage from Gaussian boson sampling. Here we prove polynomial small ball anticoncentration for complex Gaussian transpose Gram hafnians and complex symmetric Gaussian hafnians. For a k × 2n matrix X with independent standard complex Gaussian entries, we establish polynomial small ball anticoncentration for haf(XᵀX) under k ≥ 4n and n²/k = O(log n). For hafnians of 2n × 2n complex symmetric Gaussian matrices, polynomial small ball anticoncentration holds for every n ≥ 1. In both ensembles, any prescribed inverse polynomial failure probability can be achieved with an inverse polynomial small ball radius, uniformly over all centers. These results go beyond moment based anticoncentration by controlling the probability of small hafnian amplitudes. The proof combines Fourier compression with conditional Wishart geometry to handle dependent hafnian cofactors. Files: main.pdf contains the main article (14 pages); supplement.pdf contains the supplementary proofs and additional results (33 pages). Related Lean verification sources: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22554594 and https://github.com/HongruZhao/ComplexGramHafnians.
items.title: Local Anticoncentration for Gaussian Boson Sampling via Conditional Wishart Geometry

items.summary: Graph-enhanced multi-agent systems (G-MAS) coordinate large language model agents through communication graphs and role assignments, which determine how agents exchange information and divide responsibilities. However, final-score comparisons across systems combine differences in models, communication patterns, roles, and computation costs, making performance differences difficult to attribute to specific communication structures, role assignments, and information flows. To address this evaluation attribution problem, we introduce OpenMAS-GCom, a benchmark for diagnosing how these components affect G-MAS performance through controlled interventions. We represent systems through collaboration units, communication links, shared intermediate information, and execution rules. OpenMAS-GCom compares original systems with versions modified by changing one component while keeping tasks, models, prompts, and budget limits fixed. We rewire communication edges, remove specialist or critic agents, replace intermediate messages with incorrect content, and disable workers during execution. The benchmark evaluates 17 single-agent, ordinary multi-agent, and graph-enhanced configurations on 29 datasets across six domains. We add 400 G-MAS-Complex tasks requiring agents to combine information from multiple documents, resolve conflicting records, and return specified values with source identifiers. Experiments show larger mean losses after specialist removal than after critic removal, different performance degradation under incorrect messages and worker failures despite similar original scores, and different configurations achieving the highest accuracy and accuracy per token on G-MAS-Complex.
items.title: OpenMAS-GCom. A Diagnostic Benchmark for Graph-enhanced Multi-Agent Systems

items.summary: This paper presents a comprehensive framework for robot manipulation failure analysis that includes binary failure detection, failure categorization, explanation generation, and the additional capability of failure onset localization, which aims to identify the earliest moment at which a robot execution deviates from a valid task-completion trajectory and is ultimately followed by task failure. To address these tasks, we propose ProTracer, a training-free framework that leverages existing Vision-Language Models (VLMs) together with proprioceptive signals for failure analysis. Our method uses proprioceptive dynamics to identify temporally informative action boundaries and converts richer robot-state signals into structured natural-language descriptions that can be jointly analyzed together with visual observations by the VLM. This design combines the temporal precision of proprioceptive signals with the multimodal reasoning capabilities of modern VLMs without requiring additional model training. We further introduce FailTime, a benchmark with synchronized visual and proprioceptive observations for evaluating conventional failure diagnosis tasks as well as failure onset localization. Experiments demonstrate that ProTracer achieves strong performance across both conventional failure diagnosis tasks and the newly introduced failure onset localization task, highlighting the importance of proprioceptive reasoning for fine-grained temporal failure analysis.
items.title: ProTracer: Proprioception-Guided Failure Diagnosis in Robot Manipulation

items.summary: Multimodal large language models, or MLLMs, perform well at visual understanding and structured generation, yet these capabilities do not establish whether an engineering design will work when executed. Existing benchmarks assess spatial reasoning, structural validity, or physics-grounded construction, but they do not determine whether MLLMs can synthesize complete load-bearing structures and repair them after simulator execution exposes a failure. We introduce PolyBridgeBench, an executable benchmark for multimodal bridge design. A model receives a visual scene and structured engineering constraints and generates a complete node--member--material topology. Deterministic legality checks gate execution in a native dynamic physics simulation. Following an execution failure, the benchmark returns temporal visual evidence from the failed rollout and evaluates repair under a fixed interaction budget. Separate measurements of deterministic validity, dynamic functional success, and post-failure recovery identify the stage at which design fails. Experiments with six representative MLLMs across 189 levels expose a substantial gap between deterministic validity and dynamic success, pronounced sensitivity to material budgets, and limited post-failure recovery under the primary strict-budget setting.
items.title: PolyBridgeBench: Benchmarking Multimodal LLMs for Physics-Grounded Bridge Design

items.summary: Code and frozen experimental data accompanying the accepted JCDL 2026 paper A Provenance-First Discovery Layer for Research Gaps, Limitations, and Future Directions in ETDs . The system proposes research-gap, limitation, and future-direction passages from electronic theses and dissertations, aligns retained passages to source text and physical PDF pages, and keeps proposed type and synopsis separately reviewable. Version 1.0.0 includes the implementation, prompts, schemas, evaluation tools, and 31,486 frozen data files: compiled source text and corpus metadata, study splits, model outputs, reference construction, passage audits, the 600-record human-review ledger, training traces, and expected results. The code archive and checksum-pinned data archive support CPU reproduction of the reported statistics, including the original 20,000-resample whole-ETD bootstrap intervals. Fresh model training, inference, and external audits are separate operations; source PDFs and model weights are not included. items.title: A Provenance-First Discovery Layer for Research Gaps, Limitations, and Future Directions in ETDs — Code and Data

items.summary: We present an HTTP threat detection system embedded in a production reverse proxy that achieves sub-500ns per-request inference latency. The system combines a depth-limited CART decision tree with a compact two-layer MLP in an ensemble architecture, where the tree provides fast-path classification and the MLP refines uncertain cases. Model weights are exported as Rust `const` arrays, enabling zero-allocation deployment with no runtime deserialization. We formalize structural safety properties of the ensemble in the Lean~4 theorem prover, establishing a three-tier verification approach covering structural invariants, weight-dependent decision bounds, and floating-point error propagation. In initial small-scale trials on a combined dataset of production logs, CSIC-2010, and CIC-IDS2017-derived features, the ensemble achieves >99% validation accuracy for both scanner and DDoS detection, with tree inference completing in under 2ns and full ensemble inference under 6ns. We discuss limitations of the current training data and outline directions for scaling to larger, human-labeled corpora.
items.title: Sub-Microsecond HTTP Threat Detection with Decision Tree–MLP Ensembles and Lean 4 Verification

items.summary: This dataset contains analysis-ready spatial data on informal urban conditions, heat and flood exposure, slum population, and malaria burden across sub-Saharan Africa.   The deposit includes a processed subnational dataset with 4,320 administrative units, a 44-feature country/region boundary layer, annual HI406 and WBGT30 heat-exposure rasters for 2011–2020, a slum-population raster, a complete data dictionary, descriptive statistics, raster metadata, provenance documentation, rights guidance, and integrity checksums.   The vector data are provided as ESRI Shapefiles and the gridded data as GeoTIFF files. All spatial datasets use WGS 84 (EPSG:4326). The raster grids contain 1,141 columns by 1,235 rows at approximately 0.060362 degrees per cell.   The malaria indicators are population-weighted estimates mapped from source administrative-unit means onto the common slum-population grid. The original upstream flood and malaria source layers are not redistributed in this record. Users should consult the included README, data dictionary, provenance documentation, sources and limitations, and data-use notes before reuse.   This record contains data and data documentation only. Code, notebooks, manuscripts, figures, and supplementary documents are maintained separately in the project repository: https://github.com/JinRuii/informal-urban-climate-malaria-ssa
items.title: Analysis-ready spatial data on informal urban conditions, climate exposure and malaria burden across sub-Saharan Africa

items.summary: Split-Zero cohomology and the zeta-function research programme is a cumulative collection of mathematical papers, complete LaTeX proofs, formalization sources, calculations and literature-based research notes. Its central question is how the zeros of the Riemann zeta function can be studied through explicitly constructed arithmetic cohomology, spectral actions and quantitative metric estimates. The collection also retains the related heat-flow, arithmetic-trace, fluid, complexity and thermal-geometry investigations from which parts of this programme developed. Project and reading guide · Research contents · Machine-readable workbench index . Papers remain separate readable PDFs; the source archives supply the corresponding editable mathematics and supporting materials. What the collection contains Split-Zero coefficients, geometry and cohomology. The construction retains a ring's internal zero and a separate symbol for absence, so a zero element in a specified support fibre is not confused with an absent fibre. The papers construct coefficient maps, quotients, homology, finite spectral jets and their relation to the infinite theta quotient. Deligne's Weil II provides a motivating source for the cohomology–duality–weight-control programme; its finite-field theorem is not asserted to apply automatically to the Riemann zeta function. Read the cohomology and weight-control paper and the foundational objects and maps . Arithmetic theta sources and analytic control. The central analytic complex is [V → B], with theta map Θ and quotient B/ΘV. Scaling acts by D = −x∂x; the Mellin-side arithmetic function is 2ξ(s), where ξ is the completed Riemann zeta function. The papers carry finite zero packets, including multiplicities, through the original source maps and least-norm quotient metrics. They develop source recovery, residue and period maps, tensor and exterior constructions, Mellin and Gamma estimates, orthogonal-polynomial kernels, Hankel–Toda determinant identities, boundary terms, and growing-degree volume and covariance calculations. The cumulative Split-Zero reader , its proof companion , and the separate kernel, conductor and source-transport papers retain the complete arguments. Conductor geometry and spectral observation. Further papers calculate the original relation and conductor maps, kernels, quotient volumes, real-period resonances, inverse spectra and finite observation bounds. The native spectral paper , real-period paper , resonance-direction paper and inverse-power observation paper have distinct, explicit scopes. Geometric examples are not represented as identified arithmetic zeta-zero packets. Formalization and reproducible calculation. The Lean sources and formalization notes cover specified algebraic, quotient and homological interfaces. Source packages retain exact finite checkers, numerical or interval calculations where supplied, figures, manifests and verification records. A Lean check of an interface, a finite algebra test and an analytic proof are documented as different forms of evidence; none silently certifies the others. The wider zeta literature and connected investigations. The separate zeta reader , fluid/Navier–Stokes reader , de Bruijn–Newman heat-flow reader , Connes/arithmetic-trace reader , geometric-complexity reader and vacuum and thermal-geometry reader preserve the earlier research routes and their stated limitations. Related Unified Flow calculations concern specified black-hole, thermal, spectral-zeta and geometric-flow probes. The CUE research map connects existing random-unitary-matrix, Mellin and finite-phase-space work. An analogy or proposed connection is not presented as an established implication between major conjectures. How to read and assess the work This is an ongoing research programme, not a claimed proof or disproof of RH or the other major conjectures discussed in the connected notes. The remaining arithmetic estimates and identifications are stated in the individual paper
items.title: Split-Zero cohomology and the zeta-function research programme

items.summary: Resumen La diversidad de formas utilizadas para registrar los campos de autor y afiliación constituye uno de los principales problemas que afectan la normalización de los datos bibliográficos y, en consecuencia, el tiempo de procesamiento, la fiabilidad de los indicadores métricos y la delimitación del corpus utilizado en los análisis bibliométricos. En este contexto, el presente trabajo tiene como objetivo proponer los requerimientos necesarios para mejorar los procesos de normalización de datos en software destinado al análisis métrico de información científica. Para ello, se realizó un diagnóstico de los principales métodos y técnicas empleados internacionalmente para la normalización y desambiguación de datos bibliográficos. Como resultado, se establecen los requerimientos para el desarrollo de una aplicación automatizada de preprocesamiento de datos orientada a estudios métricos. La propuesta contempla la estructura de la base de datos, las tareas y etapas del procesamiento, así como los algoritmos que deberán integrarse en la aplicación. En particular, se plantea la combinación de diferentes algoritmos para abordar la desambiguación de los campos de autor y afiliación institucional. La propuesta busca contribuir al desarrollo de herramientas más eficientes y confiables para el preprocesamiento de datos en estudios bibliométricos. Palabras clave: normalización de datos; desambiguación de autores; normalización de afiliaciones; procesamiento de datos; bibliometría; minería de datos; análisis bibliométrico; preprocesamiento de datos. Abstract The diversity of formats used to record author and affiliation fields represents one of the main challenges affecting the normalization of bibliographic data and, consequently, processing time, the reliability of metric indicators, and the delimitation of the corpus used in bibliometric analyses. In this context, this study aims to propose the requirements needed to improve data normalization processes in software designed for the metric analysis of scientific information. To this end, a diagnosis was conducted of the main methods and techniques used internationally for the normalization and disambiguation of bibliographic data. As a main result, the study establishes the requirements for the development of an automated data preprocessing application for metric studies. The proposal specifies the database structure, processing tasks and stages, as well as the algorithms to be integrated into the application. In particular, it proposes combining different algorithms to address the disambiguation of author and institutional affiliation fields. The proposed approach aims to contribute to the development of more efficient and reliable tools for data preprocessing in bibliometric studies. Keywords: data normalization; author disambiguation; affiliation normalization; data processing; bibliometrics; data mining; bibliometric analysis; data preprocessing.
items.title: Requerimientos para mejorar la normalización de datos en software de análisis métricos de la información

items.summary: Supplementary material for the manuscript Li Bai Says Xiangsi and Du Fu Does Not: Idioms of Longing in Tang Poetry and the Lexical Basis of an Emotion Label by Zizheng Lv (Honours Program, Department of Asian Studies, University of British Columbia). The study asks what the yearning label of the Chinese Classical Poetry Dataset (CCPD) measures when a classifier trained on it rates Li Bai far above Du Fu. On held-out benchmark poems the label is recoverable from the words xiangsi (相思) and xiangyi (相忆); in a source-audited corpus of 52,253 Tang poems, xiangsi is followed as a formula with a history, from pre-Tang song to Tang poems of farewell and exchange, across 116 poets, and into fifteen close readings. Contents of Supplementary_Material.zip data/poems_table.parquet : the 52,253 author-eligible, CCPD-training-disjoint Tang poems (chinese-poetry, MIT) with source pointers, normalized and original bodies, poem families, surface forms, the frozen classifier's yearning probability and decision, per-poem counts of the words in the lexicon of longing, and title flags. data/author_dates.csv , data/author_dates_by_poem.csv , data/author_date_supplement.json : author dating for the Tang diachrony (Chinese Text Project Data Wiki plus listed corrections). data/xiangsi_poems_by_title_type.csv , data/dufu_yi_news_poems_by_title_type.csv : every title behind the title-type analyses with its rule-based type. data/literary_case_register.json : source-linked records for the fifteen readings. evidence/ : the numbers behind every figure and statement (benchmark counts and coefficients, corpus rates, lexicon rates with family-bootstrap intervals, diachrony, position, addressee, per-character logit attributions, form standardization, per-author tables for 116 poets, song-title rates). contextual_comparison/ : protocol and results of the three GuwenBERT fine-tuning runs. provenance/ : source versions, permissions, licenses, historical sources, and SHA-256 hashes of the archive inputs. scripts/ , figure_source/ : analysis and rendering code; requirements.txt lists the versions used. file_manifest.json and verify_results.py : SHA-256 integrity check for every distributed file (run python verify_results.py ). What runs from this package. scripts/b_e1_lexicon.py , scripts/d_e3_e4_e6.py and scripts/g_e7_all_poets.py recompute their evidence files from the distributed poem table, and figure_source/render_figures.py renders Figures 1 to 6 from the evidence files. scripts/c_e2_diachrony.py and scripts/h_e8_southern_song.py additionally require the Daizhige transcription of Lu Qinli's pre-Tang anthology and the CText Data Wiki RDF release; scripts/e_e5_attribution.py requires the fitted CCPD pipeline; scripts/a_build_table.py documents how the poem table was derived from the archive. These inputs are third-party or too large to redistribute; the README section External inputs gives their expected locations, and each script stops with a message naming any missing input. Licensing. items.summary: Self-contained synthetic seismic–gravity inversion models, Python operators, seeds, archived and profile-initialized fits, regional controls, posterior samples, figures and validation records for the manuscript by Emilson P. Leite and Maiara M. Gonçalves. Version 0.11 adds a four-start calibration on 96 paired noise comparisons, an audit of unchanged displayed seismic median errors, exact n=32 coverage intervals, and empirical bias–variance accounting of the existing regional controls. The four-start shortcut did not reproduce the profile solutions; the manuscript retains 32 profile-initialized noise pairs for each free-geometry configuration. Fixed-geometry ensembles retain 256 realizations. Wide local intervals under a free trend coexist with systematic target-property errors directed towards the prior. No new posterior chains were generated in this revision. Field observations and third-party BP-model data are not required.
items.title: When gravity adds useful information to interpretation-conditioned post-stack seismic inversion: reproducibility archive

items.summary: Traditional unsupervised anomaly detection (UAD) methods are designed to flag or localise deviations from a normative distribution, ignoring the underlying generative mechanisms of the anomalies. Yet the nature of an anomaly is often as important as its presence. We reformulate UAD as a Bayesian inverse problem, in which the objective is to infer the most probable corruption responsible for each observation. Our framework yields a probabilistic anomaly score as the energy of the inferred corruption parameters, and serves as a principled recipe for developing new UAD algorithms. We derive several existing methods as instances of the general framework, each corresponding to the same energy score under different modelling choices. Experimentally, we study the framework's components in a controlled setting, and improve object-class AUROC on the MVTec AD dataset by 2.3% by adapting the underlying corruption model. Finally, we validate the framework on a brain MRI benchmark, achieving strong detection performance while producing estimates of pathology intensity, bias, and geometry. Code is available at https://github.com/jgmyles/inverse-uad.
items.title: A Principled Approach to Unsupervised Anomaly Detection

items.summary: Hamiltonian normalizing flows are attractive generative models because their phase-space maps are invertible and volume preserving, but most neural constructions are formulated in Euclidean space. We introduce Riemannian Neural Hamiltonian Flows, which combine the fixed kinetic energy of a Riemannian manifold, a learned scalar potential, and an explicit geodesic leapfrog integrator. Our analysis explains how the learned Hamiltonian can be made interpretable. Every normalizable potential defines an implicit profile, and the position marginal initially accelerates along the relative score between that profile and the base. The matched potential is the interpretable specialization for which the implicit profile is the target. In the isotropic Gaussian case, the mechanism corresponds to a phase-space rotation. A local harmonic analysis extends this result around each mode of a general target on a manifold. The gap between the learned and the matched potential is the sum of a residual memory of the base and a bias of the model, and the two potentials agree when the position base has been transferred to the momentum. This can be achieved when the former is broader than the target. Numerical experiments on Euclidean, hyperbolic, and spherical spaces show competitive sample quality and numerical cost against a Riemannian continuous normalizing flow, and confirm the interpretability of the learned potential.
items.title: Riemannian Neural Hamiltonian Flows: Geodesic Symplectic Transport and Interpretability

items.summary: Reproducibility archive for a fully computational study of a coupled interface-mode multilayer sensing refractive index and temperature over a 100 K range, accompanying the article "Bias-Aware Detection Limits, Calibration Transfer and Matched-Control Robustness Assessment in Dual-Parameter Photonic Refractive-Index and Temperature Sensing: A Coupled Interface-Mode Multilayer Case Study" by Agah Oktay Ertay and Muhammed Mustafa Ertay, accepted by Sensors (MDPI) on 18 September 2026. It carries version 1.2.0, which the Data Availability Statement of the article names, without changing any number, table, input, model, or analysis script (560 of 572 files byte for byte; the 12 replaced root documents are kept under provenance/v1.2.0/). The 483 source, input, result, figure, and solver files of version 1.1.0 are carried byte for byte; only the root metadata files and the launcher were updated, and the v1.1.0 metadata and checksum manifest are kept under provenance/v1.1.0/. A single launcher runs the integrity check, the full reproduction, the revision stage, or both; a SHA-256 manifest covers every other file in the archive. Code is released under the MIT License (LICENSE-CODE); data, result tables, and figures under CC-BY-4.0 (LICENSE-DATA). The three measured ITO n,k tables are third-party public-domain data (CC0 1.0, via refractiveindex.info, originating from Minenkov et al., ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces 16, 9517-9531, 2024) and should be cited from that source. The study is numerical. No multilayer was fabricated and no spectrum measured; agreement between independent solvers is not offered as experimental validation.
items.title: Bias-Aware_Detection_Limits_Calibration_Transfer_and_Matched-Control_Robustness_Assessment_in_Dual-Parameter_Photonic_Refractive-Index_and_Temperature_Sensing_A_Coupled_Interface-Mode_Multilayer_Case_Study_All_Software_Package_and_Data_v1.2.1

items.summary: The collinear-antiferromagnetic spin-fluctuation paradigm has long guided unconventional superconductivity research, yet fails to reconcile the noncollinear spin phenomena observed across cuprates, iron-based superconductors, and nickelates. Using extensive first-principles calculations and unbiased large-scale DMRG simulations, we show that Dzyaloshinski-Moriya interaction (DMI)-arising from local inversion-symmetry breaking-is a common ingredient across these families. This DMI unifies hallmark observations in parent compounds-incommensurate orders, spin-wave gaps, and noncollinear textures. Under hole doping, strong DMI drives spin vortices to merge with pi-shifted hole stripes, forming hybrid vortex-hole stripe phases. These phases stabilize charge order while supporting, not suppressing, superconductivity. By contrast, under electron doping, these vortices pin holes and suppress long-range superconductivity. Our results establish DMI as a unifying link between noncollinear magnetism and superconductivity, identifying hole-strip-vortex coupling as a microscopic pairing engine. Given that DMI is common across major superconductor families, these findings challenge the prevailing pairing mechanism and offer an experimentally testable roadmap for materials optimization.
items.title: Universal Dzyaloshinski-Moriya interaction dictates pairing in unconventional superconductor families

items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) have achieved state-of-the-art performance across a wide range of tasks, motivating two important aspects of deployment: inference efficiency and output provenance, which can be tackled by speculative sampling and watermarking, respectively. However, recent works have shown that combining these two goals is highly nontrivial and can be potentially impossible. In this work, we develop a novel multi-draft speculative sampling algorithm based on Poisson processes that improves the frontier of this fundamental trade-off. The proposed algorithm has strong sampling efficiency on its own and, more interestingly, is naturally watermarkable: we can embed an unbiased watermark without degrading speculative acceptance. Moreover, our algorithm is based on an exact list-coupling-without-communication scheme, which yields a drafter invariance property that benefits both sampling and watermarking. It is the first multi-draft, drafter-invariant speculative sampling scheme that maintains both watermark strength and sampling efficiency, and we experimentally verify its strong performance in both aspects.
items.title: Watermarkable Multi-Draft Speculative Sampling via Poisson Processes
